text: Debugging is a key skill in programming. When your code doesn't work, the first step is identifying bugs—finding out exactly what is wrong and where. This can be tricky, so developers often use debugging tools, like breakpoints and step-by-step execution, to pause the program and check what is happening. A systematic approach is also important: test one part at a time, make changes, and see the results. Another helpful method is logging, which means adding messages to your code that show what it is doing. By combining these strategies, you can find and fix errors more quickly and improve your code.
